To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) aerosol kernel functions are able to provide information on the aerosol profile variations in the oxygen A band, (b) the kernels within the oxygen A-band region are better suited for aerosol profile retrieval than those outside the band, and (c) the kernels computed with 20-cM(-1) spectral resolutions are better suited for profile retrieval than those computed at lower resolutions.

the kernels within the oxygen A-band spectral region are able to provide more accurate and detailed information on the aerosol extinction profiles than the kernels in the spectral intervals outside the absorption bands.
the aerosol profile retrieval is feasible in the oxygen A band, and the new kernel functions provide better accuracy and more information than previously reported kernel functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrieval of aerosol profiles from reflected radiation in molecular absorption bands, with emphasis on the oxygen A band.
the retrieval of the aerosol extinction profiles from satellite radiance measurements within the oxygen A-band region.
the development of a method to retrieve aerosol extinction profiles from reflected radiation measurements in the oxygen A band.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the oxygen absorption A band, the retrieval of aerosol extinction profile variations from radiance measurements is possible, and the retrieval accuracy is better than that obtained from measurements outside molecular absorption bands.

, in spite of the fact that the oxygen A-band kernels are not as good as the red and near-IR kernels, they are still good enough to be used for aerosol profiling from satellite observations in this spectral region.
the new kernels are able to provide better profile retrieval results in the oxygen A band than the previous kernels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, with increasing spectral resolution, aerosol profile retrieval becomes more accurate and the aerosol extinction coefficient at the top of the atmosphere becomes more sensitive to the variations in aerosol extinction profile.
the kernels are able to provide a good estimate of the aerosol profile in the troposphere with a good accuracy, but the information content decreases rapidly with altitude.
a good knowledge of the kernel functions is essential to the retrieval of aerosol profile from radiance measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the retrieval of aerosol profiles from satellite measurements, the spectral resolution of the measurements should be as high as possible, even if this implies that the retrieval process will have to be done with a reduced number of spectral channels, since the kernels are much better conditioned in that case.
the retrieval accuracy of the extinction profile is better than that of the optical thickness profile.
, in the presence of molecular absorption, the aerosol profile is not uniquely defined by the measured radiance, and the kernel functions are not unique either.
